title: Africa · breeds of the continent
blurb: The Horn of Africa and the Nile: ticked coats, spots and the wildcat itself, from which every domestic cat on this page descends.

items.d: The ticked cat of Ethiopia, one of the oldest breeds, with a ruddy coat and an inquisitive manner.
The longhaired Abyssinian, from the Horn of Africa, with a fox-like brush tail.
Egypt's spotted cat, the only natural breed with a spotted tabby coat and the fastest domestic cat.
A Kenyan forest cat from the Arabuko-Sokoke forest, with a ticked coat and no tail problems.
The desert cat of the Gulf, recognised in 2008 from the street cats of the Arabian peninsula.
A jungle-cat hybrid from Egypt's delta, bred in the United States as a tall, athletic shorthair.
The ancestor of the house cat: a sandy tabby of Africa and the Middle East, still happy to live alone.
One of the smallest cats, 1–2 kg, and one of the most effective hunters in southern Africa.
